title: Vocabulary: topic collocations for common IELTS themes
status: Owner approved v1.0.0 on 2026-10-26; teacher release to all eligible schools (optional vocabulary lesson)
rights: Original Brains Heist LLC instructional material, AI-assisted. Passages, people and data are fictional and created for practice. Not official IELTS material. Human editorial and classroom review recommended.
prerequisites: Lesson 15 (Task 2 under time) or Lesson 16 (Speaking Part 3).
Learners have written at least one Task 2 essay.
Optional vocabulary lesson: use when learners have ideas about common topics but lack the precise phrases to express them.

objectives.text: Use 18 high-value collocations for six frequent IELTS topics: environment, health, education, work, technology and cities.
Recognise the same collocations when they are paraphrased in Reading and Listening.
Use topic collocations accurately in Speaking Part 3 and Writing Task 2 without forcing them.

levels.foundation: Learn three collocations per topic for two topics of your choice.
levels.core: Complete all tasks; use six collocations from three different topics in the discussion.
levels.extension: Use each collocation in both a spoken and a written sentence.
levels.high_band: In the discussion, combine two collocations in one developed answer with a reason and an example.

word_bank.meaning: cut the gases that cause warming / energy from wind, sun, water
word_bank.example: Switching to renewable energy would reduce carbon emissions.

word_bank.meaning: animals at risk of extinction / where they naturally live
word_bank.example: Deforestation destroys the natural habitat of endangered species.

word_bank.meaning: a way of life with little physical activity
word_bank.example: Office work often leads to a sedentary lifestyle.

word_bank.item: a balanced diet / boost the immune system
word_bank.meaning: food with the right variety / make the body better at fighting illness
word_bank.example: A balanced diet can boost the immune system.

word_bank.meaning: gain useful abilities / learning throughout life
word_bank.example: Apprenticeships help young people acquire practical skills.

word_bank.meaning: results at school / education that develops many abilities
word_bank.example: Sport contributes to a well-rounded education.

word_bank.meaning: confidence you will not lose your job / time for both work and private life
word_bank.example: Remote work can improve work-life balance.

word_bank.meaning: pay as good as other employers / chances of progress
word_bank.example: Graduates look for career prospects as well as a competitive salary.

word_bank.meaning: the most advanced technology / no longer be used
word_bank.example: Many devices become obsolete within a few years.

word_bank.meaning: too many vehicles on roads / buses, trains and trams
word_bank.example: Expanding the public transport network can ease traffic congestion.

word_bank.meaning: homes people can pay for / uncontrolled spread of a city

word_bank.example: New cycle lanes could ease congestion.
The internet has had a profound impact on education.

stages.title: Opening challenge: which word goes with which?
stages.student: Decide which sentence uses natural English.
stages.say: Some words simply belong together. Learn them as pairs.
stages.check: Learners say why 'make a balanced diet' is unnatural.

stages.title: Word bank: six topics
stages.student: In pairs, take one topic each and teach your partner its collocations with an example.
stages.teacher: Monitor pronunciation of sedentary, habitat, obsolete, congestion.
stages.check: Learners can give the partner word for ten collocations.

stages.title: Complete the collocations
stages.student: Choose the word that completes each collocation.
stages.teacher: Five minutes; reveal and drill the full phrase.
stages.say: Say the whole phrase when you check.

stages.title: Collocations in a reading summary
stages.student: Complete the summary using words from the box. The summary paraphrases the passage.
stages.teacher: Ten minutes timed. During the reveal, show the paraphrase for each gap.
stages.say: The summary uses different words from the passage; match the meaning.
stages.check: Learners show evidence for each answer.

stages.title: Part 3 discussion
stages.student: Discuss two questions in pairs; use at least four collocations naturally.
stages.teacher: Pairs, four minutes per question set. Listen live for natural use and forced use.
stages.say: Use a collocation only when it says exactly what you mean.
stages.check: Each learner uses four collocations accurately.

stages.title: Compare with the model
stages.student: Read the model answer; underline each collocation and its reason or example.
stages.teacher: Highlight how the model develops each collocation with a reason.
stages.say: The model is illustrative, not a target band.
stages.check: Learners find six collocations in the model.

stages.title: Exit ticket and homework
stages.student: Complete the exit ticket and note the homework.
stages.say: Add three collocations to your notebook every week.
stages.check: Every learner writes collocations for two topics from memory.

blocks.title: Which word goes with which?
blocks.mode: Opening challenge; learners decide before the reveal
blocks.instructions: Three learners wrote about healthy living. Which sentence sounds most natural?

examples.label: Learner A
examples.text: People should make a balanced diet and do a healthy life.
examples.comment: Unnatural: we 'eat' or 'have' a balanced diet and 'lead' a healthy life.

examples.label: Learner B
examples.text: People who lead a sedentary lifestyle should try to eat a balanced diet and exercise regularly.
examples.comment: Best: three natural collocations used accurately.

examples.label: Learner C
examples.text: People with a sitting lifestyle need an equal food.
examples.comment: Wrong words: the collocations are 'sedentary lifestyle' and 'balanced diet'.

blocks.title: Complete the collocations
blocks.mode: Controlled practice; word bank closed for core and above
blocks.instructions: Choose the word, A, B or C, that completes each collocation.

a ______ lifestyle (little exercise)

blocks.title: Collocations in a reading summary
blocks.mode: Timed practice under test-like conditions: ten minutes, no dictionary
blocks.instructions: Complete the summary using the words in the box. Write the correct letter, A–H. Three letters are not used. List of words: A sedentary; B renewable; C congestion; D affordable; E security; F emissions; G obsolete; H sprawl

stimulus.title: The fifteen-minute city
paragraphs: Urban planners in several countries are promoting the idea of the 'fifteen-minute city', in which residents can reach work, schools, shops and parks within a quarter of an hour on foot or by bicycle. Supporters argue that the model could ease traffic congestion and reduce carbon emissions, since fewer people would need to drive.

The concept also responds to concerns about health. Researchers have linked long car journeys to a sedentary lifestyle, and walking or cycling to everyday destinations is seen as a simple way of building exercise into daily routines.

Critics, however, warn that the model may be difficult to apply in areas affected by urban sprawl, where homes, workplaces and services are far apart. Others fear that improvements to neighbourhoods could push up property prices and make affordable housing even harder to find.

items.prompt: Advocates believe the approach could reduce (1) ______ on the roads.
It might also help to lower (2) ______.
Long drives have been associated with an inactive, or (3) ______, way of life.
The model may not suit places where a city has spread out without control, known as urban (4) ______.
There are also fears that it could become harder to find (5) ______ homes.
items.evidence: make affordable housing even harder to find

blocks.title: Part 3 discussion with collocations
blocks.mode: Pair practice; live feedback from partner and teacher
blocks.instructions: Discuss each question for about two minutes. Use at least four collocations from the word bank, each with a reason or example.
prompts: How has technology changed the way people work in your country?
What can governments do to encourage people to live more healthily?
Do you think cities will become better or worse places to live in the future?
blocks.routine: Speaker answers (reason + example); listener notes each collocation and whether it was natural; swap after each question.
blocks.observation: Teacher judges vocabulary from what is heard live in pair discussion; pronunciation comments are limited to what was heard live.

models.label: Illustrative Part 3 answer (not a certified band answer)
models.text: I think technology has had a profound impact on working life in my country. On the one hand, cutting-edge technology like video calls means that many office workers can now work from home, which can improve their work-life balance because they spend less time commuting. On the other hand, it also raises privacy concerns, since some companies monitor their employees' computers, and I'd say it reduces job security in certain industries, because some tasks are now done automatically. So overall, it's brought real benefits, but people may need to acquire new practical skills just to keep up.

blocks.title: Homework: topic collocations
blocks.mode: Homework; checked at the start of the next lesson
blocks.instructions: Complete each collocation with ONE word.

items.prompt: Many animals lose their natural ______ when forests are cut down.
A ______ diet includes fruit, vegetables and protein.
Many graduates choose jobs with good career ______.
Older phones quickly become ______ when new models appear.
Studying music and sport gives children a well-______ education.
Building more homes could ______ the housing shortage.

exit_ticket: One collocation for each of three topics:
A collocation I used wrongly before today, and the correct version:
The topic I need more words for:

blocks.title: Fresh check: topic collocations
blocks.instructions: Questions 1-4: complete each sentence with ONE word. Questions 5-6: choose the most natural sentence, A, B or C.

items.prompt: Solar and wind power are both forms of ______ energy.
Many workers value job ______ more than a high salary.
Improving bus and train services would strengthen the public transport ______.
Regular exercise can ______ the immune system.
Which sentence is most natural?
items.reason: A and C use wrong words.
options: A  Tigers are a dangered species.
B  Tigers are an endangered species.
C  Tigers are a danger species.

B  Adults should make all-life learning.
C  Lifelong learning helps adults adapt to new jobs.
